_doc: GSSK Household Budget — OVERVIEW diagram. Key stores, inputs and outputs only. Loadable in gssk-dia. The point of this diagram is the corrected expense ontology: an expense is a BOUNDARY TRANSACTION with a counterparty, expressed as Odum's transaction diamond (exchange node), not an edge into a sink. Compare docs/diagrams/household-detailed.json for the full network.

_legend.inputs: employer, market, grid — sources crossing INTO the household boundary
_legend.transaction_diamonds: grocery_buy, power_buy — exchange nodes coupling money out to real inflow

outputs.supplier_revenue: BOUNDARY CROSSING. Money that left the household to a counterparty. Not dissipation — the money still exists, in the supermarket's and the retailer's systems.
outputs.transfers_out: TRANSFER EXPENSE. Money out with no real inflow: tax, lender interest, insurance premium, bank fees.
outputs.value_lost: ACCOUNTING WRITE-DOWN. Book value depreciated. No counterparty, no physical referent.
outputs.consumed: MATERIAL USED UP. Stock depleted by household consumption.
outputs.heat: GENUINE DISSIPATION. Odum's heat sink. The only terminal node that is thermodynamically terminal.
outputs.debt_retired: Counter of principal repaid. The mortgage store is a debt counter, not a money holding.

metadata.name: Household Budget — Overview
metadata.description: Key stores, inputs and outputs of the household budget model. Expenses are modelled as exchange-node boundary transactions with counterparties, not as edges into a generic expense sink.
metadata.author: gssk-budget

nodes._role: INPUT — wage income crossing the household boundary
INPUT — counterparty supplying goods. A supermarket is a SOURCE of material, not a sink for money.
INPUT — counterparty supplying energy. The electricity retailer is a SOURCE of energy.
KEY STORE — transaction account. The hub every money flow passes through.
Pinned origin for interaction logic. REQ-FLOW-2: interest is never a self-edge.
KEY STORE — aspirational buffer. Savings held against declared goals.
KEY STORE — durable asset book value. Physical condition leg lives in the detailed diagram (REQ-ONT-1).
KEY STORE — outstanding mortgage principal. A DEBT COUNTER on the money carrier, not a money holding.
TRANSACTION DIAMOND — the grocery purchase. Money leaves the account, goods enter the pantry, coupled at the declared price. THIS is what an expense is.
TRANSACTION DIAMOND — the electricity bill. Money out, energy in. The energy is consumed on receipt and dissipates.
OUTPUT — TRANSFER EXPENSE. Tax, lender interest, insurance, fees. Money out, nothing real back. Aggregated here; decomposed per counterparty in the detailed diagram.
OUTPUT — ACCOUNTING WRITE-DOWN. Depreciation of book value. No counterparty exists on the other side of this flow.
OUTPUT — principal repaid. Drains the debt counter.
KEY STORE — consumable stock actually held by the household.
OUTPUT — BOUNDARY CROSSING. Money that has left the household into a counterparty's system. It is not dissipated; it is elsewhere.
OUTPUT — GENUINE DISSIPATION. Odum's heat sink. The only thermodynamically terminal node here.
OUTPUT — material consumed by the household.

edges._note: Fortnightly salary as a forcing waveform, not an event list (REQ-TIME-2). duty=1/14 delivers 4200 AUD on one day in fourteen. phase is a TIME offset in days and is SUBTRACTED (REQ-TIME-4).
Discretionary transfer to the goal buffer. Linear: saving scales with what is available.

Interest accrual. REQ-FLOW-2 pattern: constant node pinned at 1.0 as origin, interaction logic, principal as control_node. F = k x Q_pinned x Q_mortgage = daily rate x principal. control_node is read, never consumed.
Principal repayment drains the debt counter. threshold logic floors it at zero so the store cannot go negative.
TRANSFER EXPENSE — the cash leg. Tax, mortgage repayment cash, insurance premium, bank fees. Money out with no real inflow, so a sink IS the right terminal here. Aggregated for the overview.
Money leg IN to the grocery transaction diamond.
Goods leg IN — the supermarket supplies the transaction.
Goods leg OUT — groceries enter household stock. THIS is the leg the sink-only model discards.
Money leg OUT — payment crosses the household boundary into the supermarket's system. F_money = price x F_goods.
Household consumption depletes the stock. Linear: use proportional to stock on hand.
Money leg IN to the electricity transaction diamond.
Energy leg IN — the retailer supplies the transaction.
Energy leg OUT — electricity is a service consumed on receipt. There is no household stock, so it goes straight to genuine dissipation.
Money leg OUT — the bill crosses the boundary into the retailer's system.
Declining-balance depreciation (REQ-FLOW-1 default). Asymptotic, never negative.
